items.title: Polymarket rolls out five-minute crypto markets on its regulated US platform, CoinDesk reports
items.content_text: - **Polymarket rolls out five-minute crypto markets on its regulated US platform, CoinDesk reports** — CoinDesk reports Polymarket has started offering five-minute cryptocurrency up-or-down contracts on its regulated US platform, operated by QCX LLC under CFTC oversight, covering bitcoin, ether, solana and XRP with correct predictions paying 1 dollar per share. The US platform settles the markets using CF Benchmarks real-time dollar indexes, averaging 60 observations in the final 60 seconds, while the CFTC is examining compliance with a 2022 settlement, according to Reuters reporting cited by CoinDesk. ([CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/29/polymarket-brings-ultra-short-crypto-prediction-markets-to-u-s-platform))

items.title: USA Today analysis finds NFL share of prediction market volume rose from about 59 percent to 69 percent, USA Today reports
items.content_text: - **USA Today analysis finds NFL share of prediction market volume rose from about 59 percent to 69 percent, USA Today reports** — USA Today reports it replicated the NFL claim in an October 8 Supreme Court brief that 1.8 billion dollars of 3.3 billion dollars in prediction market trading on the first Sunday of the 2026 season was NFL-related, calculating about 59 percent of notional volume on Kalshi and Polymarket US was NFL-related on September 13. items.title: CFTC proposes writing prediction markets into swap rules while carving sportsbooks out, Unchained reports
items.content_text: - **CFTC proposes writing prediction markets into swap rules while carving sportsbooks out, Unchained reports** — Unchained reports the CFTC on October 9 proposed adding event contracts, including those based on sports, politics, cultural and weather events, to its regulatory definition of a swap at 17 CFR 1.3, while issuing a companion interim final rule keeping sportsbook and casino games outside that definition. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig said event contracts are commodity derivatives within the agency exclusive jurisdiction under the Commodity Exchange Act, and comments on the proposal are due 30 days after Federal Register publication. ([Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/cftc-writes-prediction-markets-into-swap-rules-and-carves-sportsbooks-out/))

A week ago, Andrew Novak was a 2 percent afterthought in the VidantaWorld Mexico Open winner market on Kalshi. Today he leads a 123-outcome board at 30 percent, a 27-point climb that is the biggest seven-day move on DeFi Rate's prediction-market board.

The money followed the move. The market traded $800K in the last 24 hours, running at 2.2 times its daily average, and a $100 position on Novak at the ask now pays $333 if he wins. In a field this wide, one name taking nearly a third of the probability is a statement, not a drift.

The rest of the board shows how open it still is. Ben Griffin sits second at 12 percent and Marco Penge third at 5.3 percent, leaving more than half the probability spread across the other 120 golfers. Novak is the favorite now, but the market is still pricing a race, not a coronation.

Golf outrights are a hard test for any exchange. Unlike a two-team game, a 123-outcome board has to price contenders, longshots and the field at once, and keep all of those prices honest as the tournament moves. A 27-point repricing in a single week is exactly the kind of move that test is built to catch.

That is the new shape of golf on prediction markets: a 123-name outright board repricing in real time, where a longshot can gain 27 points in a week and pull $800K of fresh trading behind him.

items.content_text:
Twelve Trades for $114.87: Utah Put Kalshi's Founders on the Charge Sheet

The evidence is small. The charges are not. Utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed a criminal complaint on October 29 naming Kalshi chief executive Tarek Mansour and chief operating officer Luana Lopes Lara as defendants, after an undercover agent placed 12 sports trades on the platform for a total of $114.87.

items.content_text:
The One-Cent Shelf: $419 Million Traded on Almost Nothing

Look at the top of the prediction-market volume board and the biggest numbers carry the smallest prices. Eight markets priced at exactly 1 cent, the floor, have traded $418,727,767 between them, according to PicksByOdds' live board on October 31. Volume, it turns out, does not require belief.

The leader is "Will Jesus Christ return before 2027?" at 1 cent on $66,761,416 traded. Next is LeBron James winning the 2028 presidential election, also 1 cent, on $54,895,306. Oprah Winfrey winning the 2028 Democratic nomination follows at 1 cent on $54,448,323, and Bernie Sanders winning the same nomination at 1 cent on $52,923,492. Those four alone account for more than $228 million.

The shelf runs deeper. Chelsea Clinton at $51,070,529, Andrew Yang at $48,953,782, Tim Walz at $44,877,007 and Hunter Biden at $44,797,912, each priced at 1 cent for the 2028 Democratic nomination or the presidency, bring the eight-market total past $418 million, none of them moving off the floor.

PicksByOdds notes much of that activity likely reflects traders selling cheap Yes shares to collect small, slow returns, not anyone expecting the outcome. A 1-cent Yes pays a dollar if it happens; the other side collects the near-certain cent, repeated at enormous scale. High volume on a longshot is still a longshot.

That is a tell about this market's maturity. The board's heaviest traffic is not always a forecast. Sometimes it is a yield trade wearing a headline, and the one-cent shelf is where prediction markets quietly became a place to park conviction that nothing will happen.

Kansas Flipped: Three Days Out, the Senate Map Moved

Three days before Election Day on November 3, the biggest move on the midterm board is not in a marquee state. In Kansas, the Democrat in the Senate race climbed from 40% to 51% in seven days on Kalshi, an 11-point jump that DeFi Rate ranks as the largest Senate move of the week. At 51 cents to 50 cents, a race traders had priced as Republican is now a coin flip that broke the other way.

That one flip is why the chamber numbers keep rising. Averaging Kalshi and Polymarket, DeFi Rate puts Democrats at 70% to take the Senate and 94% to win the House, with traders putting $24 million into election markets in the past 24 hours. Kalshi alone prices Senate control at 68% and House control at 93%, across 311 tradeable midterm contracts covering 35 Senate races and 66 competitive House districts.

The path still runs through the same states. Democrats need a net gain of four Senate seats, and DeFi Rate notes the 51st seat runs through Maine, where Troy Jackson is at 69%. Texas has moved with Kansas: James Talarico is at 71%, up 6 points in a week. Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed is at 75%, also up 6, and Minnesota's Democrat rose from 84% to 90%.

The tightest board is Iowa, where Ashley Hinson leads Josh Turek 56 cents to 45, on 7.9 million contracts traded. And the balance-of-power combo, the single bet on who controls both chambers, has traded 77.8 million contracts with 60.9 million still open. Three days out, the House looks priced in. Kansas is the reminder that the Senate is not.

items.title: SEC monitoring prediction markets for insider trading on company-linked contracts, enforcement director says, Bitcoinist reports
items.content_text: - **SEC monitoring prediction markets for insider trading on company-linked contracts, enforcement director says, Bitcoinist reports** — SEC Enforcement Director David Woodcock said the agency is closely monitoring prediction markets for insider trading, fraud and manipulation, particularly contracts tied to company earnings and performance, according to an October 29 Bloomberg report cited by Bitcoinist. Woodcock signaled future enforcement action but did not announce new charges or name a specific platform, while the SEC and CFTC continue a joint review of swap definitions. ([Bitcoinist](https://bitcoinist.com/prediction-markets-face-sec-warning-over-insider-trading/))
